item.title: Anomaly Classification System (ACS) Guide:
item.content:encoded: What I meant was that the disruption and the risk classes only describes more the influence Over people, like it was a sort of wave. But if an object is dangerous only for the knowledge that it possesses then the disruption and risk are low. That doesn’t really indicate the level of danger. We asume than the scps have a sort of wave that tends to affects people. But a brick that only grants wishes is dangerous for other reasons. But his disruption and risk would be low. So perhaps there’s a need for another level of classification.

item.title: SCP-5733:
item.content:encoded:
At the time I was using Firefox on a [Windows] laptop with 1920 x 1080 resolution.

Embarrassingly, I have to admit that I didn't properly appreciate what the end actually meant on the first read, and having been prodded by you I actually *get it* now — I'm retracting that criticism and replacing it with a much weaker "ending is perhaps not clear enough"!

item.title: SCP-5733:
item.content:encoded:
Hi! I’m glad that, on the whole, you enjoyed the article.

I’m sorry you found the CSS annoying, do you mind if I ask what device you use? I’ll bear this in mind for future articles, and try to make them more accessible.

Regarding the ending, it was planned from the start, and I tried to foreshadow the twist in the testing logs: two -1 instances appear when it’s two viewers, when viewed by a thaumaturge the -1 instance knows thaumaturgy. There were a few more obvious indications but these were removed during drafting based on feedback it made it too obvious. Thanks for taking the time to comment, i’ll look to apply your critique to my future drafts.

item.title: SCP-666½-J:
item.content:encoded:
SCP-106's femur breaker made me squeamish. Procedure 110-Montauk horrified me. And SCP-666-1/2-J is supposedly more painful than the femur breaker and Procedure 110-Montauk combined, squared. But instead of being mortified by the amount of pain described here, I'm laughing.

This is the most painful thing to exist in any fiction I have ever read, and I'm laughing!

item.title: Fox Hunt: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
Yes, there were folks in that brave era
Who had the hearts and souls of heroes:
Real men, unlike you lads!
They battled, but their luck turned ill, and
So many brave young men were killed then.
But Moscow, if God had not willed it,
Would never have changed hands!

Mikhail Lermontov, Borodino

Connecting some dots, introducing some new characters. Can't have a multi-pronged MTF without new members.

Thank you to Pedagon and as always, HarryBlank for their critique and help making this sing.
